about: Rules for the held-ground simulation (scripts/compile-front.ts). Gates: a side can take ground in a territory only from the event that opens that front, or never (fromEvent null). Anchored: in these territories a side's held ground is a band reaching in from its own border (a siege front tied to its homeland) rather than an area around its army. Each rule names its basis. Reopen: from that event a side may take again ground it lost earlier. Reach scale: a side's formations standing in that territory reach that share of their usual distance, at most maxReach of the atlas width. Minimum weight: a formation counts with at least that influence.

gates.basis: The Imperial Army has crossed the Tempest border (V13 Ch1). Before it, the column is inside the Empire and holds no Jura ground, whatever the reach of its numbers.

R7 scenario: imperial ground in Dwargon from the eastern crossing (EVT-0521): the 30,000 on the isthmus up to the Eastern Gate and the coast, and the 200,000 on their way from the south-western border to the Main Gate. Both are given back when the formations holding them are destroyed (status quo).

reopen.basis: R7 scenario: the Third Strike advances over ground the Empire lost earlier in the war (Word document, L: advancement teritorial). Until then, ground a side lost stays lost.

reachScale.basis: R7: Dwargon is mountain and isthmus country. An imperial formation standing in Dwargon reaches at most 0.011 of the atlas width (about 60 km) whatever its size, so the south-western thrust shows as a corridor to the Main Gate and the Eastern Gate front as a bridgehead on the isthmus, not as the whole kingdom.

minWeight.basis: R7 scenario: the Third Strike's Tempest group is ordered to take ground on its way to the capital (Word document, L: "advancement teritorial"). At 2,100 it would hold nothing under the strength rule; it is given the weight of a formation able to hold a bridgehead of a few tens of kilometres east of the capital garrison's reach.
